subject: Clarify p50/p95 measurement approach + temporary EU carve-out request
messages:
From: Jake Morgan <jake@edgecloud.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: EdgeCloud Legal <legal@edgecloud.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API SLOs — question on measurement and short-term carve-out request

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal/R&D teams are working through the Hosted API SLA and have two quick asks before we sign: 1) how Redwood defines the p50/p95 measurement windows for multi-tenant hosted customers (are percentiles computed globally, per-customer, or request-weighted?), and 2) we have an upcoming infra migration in our EU region on Jan 10 that may cause a 48–72h spike in latency. We need to understand whether we can get a documented, time-boxed exception/carve-out for that migration window so it doesn't count against a renewal SLO baseline.

I've attached a small sample of our traffic buckets and some example traces. Can your team propose language/measurement rules and a temporary carve-out process? Legal would like the process to be explicit (dates, measurement backfill, and whether fallback to compatible model variants is allowed).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we hope to close by EOY.

Best,
Jake Morgan
Head of Platform
EdgeCloud Systems
[Attachment: slo-measurement-examples.csv]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Jake Morgan <jake@edgecloud.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — question on measurement and short-term carve-out request

Hi Jake — thanks for the clear asks and the sample. High-level answers up front:

- Percentiles: For Hosted, we compute p50/p95 on a per-customer routing view (so your tenant's requests form the population). We also maintain a global telemetry stream for platform health, but contractual SLOs are tenant-scoped.

- Request weighting: Percentiles are computed on raw request latencies (each request is one observation). We do not weight by token count unless the customer explicitly purchases token-weighted measurement in the contract.

- Migration carve-outs: Redwood can agree to a narrowly scoped, timeboxed exception. We typically require: clear start/end dates, a windowed-backfill approach to exclude the carve-out from the rolling measurement, and a post-migration verification run where we validate traffic distribution.

Actionables: I'm looping in Marissa (Customer Success) and Ben (SRE) to draft exact wording and the measurement steps. Can you confirm the planned migration start/end and whether you'll use a temporary IP-range or VPC shift so we can validate routing impacts?

Draft attachments: 1) proposed measurement-rules sheet, 2) wording for the carve-out clause. I'll follow up with an internal note to align on the p50/p95 aggregation semantics.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slo-window-proposal.xlsx]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 13:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API SLOs — internal: draft measurement language and carve-out process

Team — forwarding Jake's note. My proposal (short):

1) Measurement population: tenant-scoped p50/p95 aggregated over request-level latencies, computed on the "inference response complete" timestamp in our edge gateways.

2) Windowing: Contract SLOs evaluate p50 over a 1-minute aggregation then roll up to 24-hour daily windows for reporting; p95 evaluated on 5-minute buckets rolled up to a 7-day window for contractual remediation. This avoids sensitivity to short transient spikes while still protecting tail latency.

3) Carve-out: For the Jan 10 migration, propose a 72-hour carve-out window (configurable start/end), excluded from the rolling measurement. Requirements: customer must notify 7 business days in advance, provide migration plan and IP/VPC changes, and allow Redwood to run a 6-hour post-migration traffic sample for verification. No backfill of the carve-out period into historical baselines for SLA calculation (i.e., excluded entirely).

4) Fallback/variants: We allow Redwood-initiated fallback to compatible model variants during the carve-out but will not count auto-fallback latencies against the carve-out if it was triggered by platform failure. If customer initiates model switch deliberately, those latencies are in-scope unless otherwise agreed.

Ben — can you confirm the feasibility of the 5-minute p95 bucket and the post-migration verification run? Rishi — advise legal wording (especially around "excluded entirely" v/s "temporary offset").

-Marissa
Senior CS Manager, Redwood Inference

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API SLOs — internal: draft measurement language and carve-out process

Marissa — technical thumbs-up with small caveats:

- 1-min p50 buckets -> fine.
- 5-min p95 buckets -> feasible but adds retention/compute for higher-resolution rolling windows; cost impact is modest for a single tenant but we'll quantify.
- Post-migration verification: we can run a 6-hour sampled comparison using the same edge proxies. Need customer's sampling flags and the VPC/IP ranges in advance.

I'll produce a short appendix describing how we treat KV/prefix cache warmups: cold-warm transitions are included in the measurement unless the customer requests specific cold-start carve-outs (rare).

Attaching a quick CSV of sample bucket behaviour from a past migration for reference.

-Ben
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: migration-sample-buckets.csv]

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Hosted API SLOs — proposed measurement rules and Jan migration carve-out

Hi Jake — thanks for the details; below is the proposal Redwood can include in the MSA appendix. If this looks acceptable we can push a DocuSign amendment and record the carve-out in the deal: DEAL-8372.

Proposal (summary):
- Measurement population: tenant-scoped request-level latencies (inference response complete).
- Percentile computation: raw request observations, unweighted by token count, computed in 1-minute buckets for p50 and 5-minute buckets for p95.
- Reporting windows: p50 reported daily (24h roll-up); p95 reported weekly (7-day roll-up) for remediation triggers.
- Jan migration carve-out: 72-hour timeboxed exclusion. Preconditions: customer notifies Redwood 7 business days prior, provides migration plan and IP/VPC ranges, and allows Redwood a 6-hour post-migration verification sample. The carve-out period will be excluded entirely from contractual SLO computations (no backfill).
- Fallbacks: Redwood may route to compatible model variants during the carve-out; such routing does not automatically null the carve-out but will be documented in the post-migration verification report.

Next steps: Jake — confirm planned migration window (start/end) and share the migration plan. Legal: we'll prepare a short DocuSign amendment and add this appendix to the MSA. I'll also include the expected cost delta for the higher-resolution p95 buckets and the SRE appendix Ben promised.

If you approve, Marissa will attach the amendment and we can sign this week.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
